summary: Every drift finding names its member by the one address grammar, so a nested member is told apart from a top-level namesake

edit.description: Five finding sites name a member by a bare name or a bare `kind:name`, which for a nested member spells an address no member wears: `DriftError::UnknownKind`'s `member` (line 1618), `AtLocusUnderWorkspace` via `host_address(&facts.name, &member.name)` (line 1632), the `host` the body/format/include refusals share (line 1685) — each with `member.host` in hand, so `payload_member_address` (line 2317) already spells them — plus two that cannot recover the host today: `FormatHasNoWriteFace` in the write closure (line 2896, off `Projection`, line 934) and the `root.fresh` projection finding (line 3236, off `RawLockRow`, line 2708). Carry the host fact into `Projection` and `RollupEntry` (line 608) and out through `rollup_tables` (line 678) as a column `walk_lock_rows_from_doc` (line 2725) lifts back, so the finding resolves the address through `crate::member_address` rather than re-spelling it. The column is absent for a top-level member: `name` keeps meaning the member's own key, so every existing reader of it (`ProvenanceRow` line 2757, `render_emit` line 3032, `src/install.rs`'s lock reads) is untouched. No committed lock moves a byte either: the only one build owns, `examples/base-harness/.temper/lock.toml`, carries rollup rows for top-level members alone (families censused this tick — `decision`, `flow`, `memory`, `rule`, `skill`, `system`, no nested-file-child row), and if a future example gained one that path is already a standing build surface, fence-free.

The proof lands beside the file-child emit tests already here (`a_file_childs_projection_composes_from_its_hosts_unit_and_the_templates_pattern`, line 380; `a_matching_file_under_a_hosts_unit_is_discovered_as_that_hosts_file_child`, line 672), which already build a host-plus-child harness and emit it.

tests.asserts: a nested file child whose committed projection is hand-edited yields a `root.fresh` finding naming the child's whole `<host-address>/<kind>/<key>` address, not its bare key; a top-level member's finding still reads `<kind>:<name>`; and two same-keyed children under different hosts yield two findings a reader can tell apart

acceptance: cargo test green, including the existing rollup-column readers (tests/it/emit.rs, tests/it/mcp_kind.rs, tests/it/local_locus.rs) unchanged; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; no finding in src/drift.rs spells a member address outside `crate::member_address`.
notes: Routed from the inbox note observed at fca7b4f9, re-verified at HEAD and widened to the verified class: the note named `root.fresh` only, four more sites spell a member the same bare way. The host is a declared payload fact (`PayloadMember.host`) reaching no rollup row, so the fresh judge cannot recover it. Re-cut after a fence revert — `.temper/lock.toml` is out of scope, not build's to re-emit. scoped at 43541de0
